overview: A tech- and AI-heavy day once the politics is filtered out. Karpathy argues the gap in understanding AI capability is widening. Coinbase says a fine-tuned 9B open model beat frontier models on fraud detection, and investors are arguing over whether AI inference is a defensible business. BillAckman, elonmusk, PalmerLuckey and horowitz_b posted mostly political content, which is skipped here.

top_items.title: karpathy - Estimates ~6B people have barely used LLMs, ~20M see agents finish month-long code projects, and ~5,000 insiders see far more
brian_armstrong - Coinbase fine-tuned Qwen3.5-9B on internal data, and he says it beat frontier models on fraud prevention at lower cost
JayaGup10 - Calls AI inference a 'permanent reverse auction' where customers switch providers with one line of code; saranormous says scale leaders win
chamath - Shares Social Capital chart: Anthropic's share of business AI token spend on Ramp fell from 69.5% in March to 51.0%; OpenAI is at 44.5%
brian_armstrong - Praises an SEC proposal for merit-based access to private markets, which could open private investing to more retail investors
brian_armstrong - Coinbase finished integrating Deribit, linking US and international crypto derivatives under one collateral pool
elonmusk - Pushes Grok Bot: a user says it found and ordered a sold-out iPhone 18 Pro Max; it now also works inside Tesla Cybercab rides
BillGates - Says AI needs safeguards like planes, cars and medicines, and told CNN we will move 'beyond self-governance' within a year
